content.text:
Write a believable imessage conversation from this scenario. Use `Me` exactly for the user's own messages and distinct names for other people. `Me` is a speaker label, never a person's name inside message bodies; use natural pronouns there. The user must speak at least once. Do not use `User`, `I`, or another alias for the user's speaker label.

Chat members: Me, Maya, Leo. Use only these speaker labels.
Conversation date: 2026-09-17. Relative dates in the conversation use this date as their reference.
These messages will be timestamped between 20:00 and 23:20 local time. Keep references to the current time of day consistent with that window.
Scenario: Leo shares a ridiculous pizza slogan he heard in a sketch, with Maya and the user reacting. Make the joke sound like a quote, not an invitation.

The conversation must naturally and unambiguously establish each of these facts (they are authoring constraints, not lines to copy):
1. Leo quotes a sketch saying 'we should get pizza on Saturday and never go back to work'. The group laughs; they make no Saturday plan.

Continue each person's voice from their earlier messages. Start with what they want to say; small talk and unrelated remarks are optional. Allow short message bursts and different reply lengths. Do not force an opening greeting, joke or tired-after-work aside into every exchange. Noise: medium. Mix the topic into ordinary daily chatter, unrelated facts and side plans. Write only text messages: no bracketed stage directions, photo placeholders, or imaginary attachment markers.

Make commitments clear, but never turn confirmations into a recital of date, time, place, and companion. A short 'yeah that works' after a specific proposal is a real acceptance. In a continuation, people can change one detail without repeating the whole existing plan. A tentative 'should be' alone is not an acceptance.

Use natural date language in casual messages. 'Friday' is enough when this conversation date makes it unambiguous; avoid month, day number, or year unless a person would actually clarify it.

Write between 60 and 120 messages. Each chat member should send 20–40 messages across this exchange. Write one message per line, as `Name: message` using consistent speaker names. No timestamps, headers, or narration inside the dialogue. Return only a JSON object with `dialogue` (one string containing the message lines) and `writer_note` (one or two sentences about the creative choices that made the conversation natural). The note is an explanation for the author, not a private reasoning transcript.

output.encrypted_content: <encrypted reasoning retained in private run artifact>

summary.text: Generating an iMessage-style dialogue with specified speakers, date, time window, and scenario while keeping references consistent and avoiding a Saturday plan.
Clarifying speaker-label rules and pronoun usage while enforcing the no-Saturday-plan constraint.
Adding a quoted sketch line as a joke while keeping the no-Saturday-plan constraint.

content.text:
{
  "dialogue": "Leo: okay you guys have to hear this sketch i just watched
Maya: lol what now
Leo: its this fake ad for a pizza place
Me: oh no
Leo: the guy is in a suit crying into a slice
Maya: relatable tbh
Leo: and he's like "we should get pizza on Saturday and never go back to work"
Maya: HAHAHA stop
Me: that's actually amazing
Leo: right?? the delivery was so serious
Maya: never go back to work i'm in
Me: same honestly, let him cook
Leo: the sketch show is that one with the two british dudes
Maya: oh i know which one you mean
Me: did they have the tiny desk and the plant?
Leo: YES exactly that one
Maya: i love their office bits
Leo: this one was new from yesterday i think
Me: send me the name after, i need background noise for dishes
Leo: will do, its like 4 mins
Maya: speaking of dishes i finally unloaded mine
Me: proud of you
Maya: took me two days lol
Leo: two days is rookie numbers
Me: how long has yours been sitting?
Leo: don't worry about it
Maya: he has a whole ecosystem in his sink
Leo: rude but accurate
Me: did you end up finishing that report today?
Maya: ugh mostly
Maya: my laptop died at like 5pm so i gave up
Leo: classic sign to log off
Me: mine was dragging all afternoon too
Leo: did IT ever get back to you?
Me: nope, still waiting
Maya: did you try turning it off and on again
Me: three times lol
Leo: that's the full IT toolkit right there
Maya: anyway i'm making tea, anyone want virtual tea
Leo: always
Me: yes please, peppermint if you have it
Maya: i only have chamomile and some weird lemon thing
Me: lemon thing works
Leo: give me the weird one
Maya: okay one weird tea for leo
Leo: back to the sketch tho, the slogan kept repeating
Me: like a jingle?
Leo: yeah in this deep movie trailer voice
Maya: never go back to workkkk
Me: hahaha stop i can hear it
Leo: exactly!!
Maya: i needed that laugh today
Me: same, thursday felt so long
Leo: thursdays always drag
Maya: tomorrow's friday tho
Me: thank god
Leo: any big friday plans?
Maya: just gym in the morning then work
Me: i'm just trying to leave on time for once
Leo: good luck with that
Maya: fr tho you always get stuck late on fridays
Me: i know, i'm gonna put my laptop away at 5 sharp
Leo: manifesting that for you
Maya: what about you leo?
Leo: probably just laundry and that game
Me: which game?
Leo: the co-op cooking one, its chaos
Maya: oh i suck at that game
Leo: you're not bad, you just set the kitchen on fire once
Maya: ONCE?? it was like three times
Me: lol i remember that
Leo: we should play tomorrow night if you're free
Maya: maybe, i'll see how tired i am after gym
Me: i might join for a round
Leo: bet, no pressure tho
Maya: did you eat yet btw?
Leo: had leftover pasta
Me: i had cereal for dinner don't judge
Maya: no judgment, cereal slaps at night
Leo: what kind?
Me: honey nut something
Leo: solid choice
Maya: i had soup and toast, very grandma of me
Me: cozy tho
Leo: it's soup weather now finally
Maya: finally! it was freezing this morning
Me: i wore my heavy jacket
Leo: me too, broke out the fall one
Maya: okay but back to that pizza line
Maya: never go back to work is my new motto
Me: put it on a t-shirt
Leo: honestly it would sell
Maya: i'd buy one
Me: me too lol
Leo: the comments were all quoting it too
Maya: as they should
Me: alright i gotta finish these dishes, talk later?
Leo: yeah, i'll send that sketch link
Maya: send it here!
Leo: will do in a sec
Me: perfect, night guys",
  "writer_note": "Framed Leo's line as a quoted sketch bit with clear attribution and over-the-top delivery, then had Maya and Me laugh it off as a motto without making any Saturday plan, burying it in normal evening chatter about work, food, and Friday."
}
